Root cause: Brevi dropped class-body annotations everywhere, and dynpy's typing pass refused every `.__annotations__` read; the typed build also cannot parse classes nested in a function, so the whole test refused to build.

Fix (dynamic build, which the normal build falls back to for nested classes):
- src/dynpy/emit.rs: class bodies now implement CPython's SETUP_ANNOTATIONS/STORE_ANNOTATION. When a class body has any annotated statement (and the module has no `from __future__ import annotations`), the emitter creates a `__annotations__` dict as the first class attribute and, at each `x: T [= v]` statement, evaluates the value first, then the annotation (CPython's order), stores simple-name annotations in the dict, and keeps the name unbound unless a value was assigned.
- src/dynpy/rt_core.rs / rt_call.rs: `Class::annotations()` and getattr special-cases give a class its own `__annotations__` only — never an inherited one — and lazily create and cache an empty dict on first read for annotation-less classes, matching CPython (including `"__annotations__" in C.__dict__` becoming true only after a read).
- src/dynpy/typing.rs: the blanket refusal is narrowed to allow `C.__annotations__` and `C().__annotations__` for program classes. Reads on functions/modules/variables, NamedTuple/TypedDict classes, `from __future__ import annotations` modules, and Brevi's own pydantic programs are still refused (they fall back to CPython rather than print something wrong).

Tested: the failing conformance test now matches CPython on both the normal and forced dynamic build (normal path runs dynamic). Also verified with try_python: annotation inheritance, value-before-annotation evaluation order, explicit `__annotations__ = {...}` rebinding, `__annotations__ = None` TypeError, dataclasses, enums, class-vs-instance reads, lazy empty-dict caching, and that function/future/NamedTuple/pydantic `__annotations__` reads still refuse.
